## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Katāpattivāra* (Pvr 1.2) is a section of the *Parivāra* in the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text systematically defines the number of sub-offences that can be incurred when a monastic rule is broken [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the text has been made by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

In computational text-reuse analysis, DharmaNexus identifies 6,425 matching passages between the *Katāpattivāra* and 195 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its most substantial internal parallels appear in other analytical segments of the *Parivāra*, especially the bhikkhunī counterpart *Katāpattivāra* (Pvr 2.2, with over 46,000 shared characters), *Katthapaññattivāra* (Pvr 1.1), and *Katāpattivāra* (Pvr 1.10), alongside the *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha*, the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha*, and post-canonical Vinaya literature including the *Vinayavinicchaya* and the *Parivāra-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].
